subject: Planned EU-West maintenance: warm-handoff window & canary booking
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: DataSure Ops <ops@datasure.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Planned maintenance: EU-West warm-handoff window (June 11)

Hi team,

Heads-up about a short, planned maintenance window in eu-west next week. We're applying a minor kernel/driver update that improves IO latency under certain heavy KV-cache patterns. To minimize impact for customers with pinned capacity or tight latency SLOs, we'll run the change as a controlled "warm-handoff" across racks with an initial canary prior to region-wide roll.

Summary:
- What: Kernel/driver compatibility update + small NIC firmware microfix.
- Why: Reduces rare IO stalls observed under long-lived KV-cache sessions; improves failover behavior.
- When (primary): Wednesday, 11 June 2025, 02:00–06:00 UTC (staged across availability zones).
- Expected impact: Sub-second or no customer-facing latency change for most workloads. Short transient throttles possible during the per-rack handoff window (~60–90s for affected instances).
- Canary: We will run a 30-minute canary in eu-west-1a at 02:00–02:30 UTC.

What we need from you:
1) If you run long-running KV-cache sessions (prefix caching, streaming inference), please flag any critical jobs that must be paused during the canary/roll (reply with job ids).
2) If you'd like us to reserve the canary for a subset of your traffic or route trial endpoints to a safe pool, tell us which subdomain/endpoints.

We've attached the runbook and a short KV-cache preservation checklist. The runbook contains rollback criteria, monitoring dashboards, and contact escalation paths. We'll broadcast live updates to https://status.redwood.inference/eu-west/2025-06-11-maintenance during the window.

Attachments:
- euw-warm-handoff-runbook.pdf (runbook + rollback plan)
- kv-cache-preservation-checklist.xlsx (customer checks to reduce cache misses)

If you'd prefer a different canary slot, let us know within 48 hours and we'll accommodate.

Thanks,

Markus Klein
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: DataSure Ops <ops@datasure.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 12:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: EU-West warm-handoff window (June 11)

Thanks, Markus — appreciate the heads-up.

A couple quick asks from our side:
- Can we book the canary to run against our staging subset only? We'll provide a prefix for routing.
- We operate long-lived prefix caches for model sessions; preserving KV-cache state is important for latency. Does your runbook include a validation step to ensure cache warmup persists after each rack handoff?

If possible, please confirm the exact time of the canary for eu-west-1a in UTC (we'll coordinate our test jobs). Also, could you share the last two graphs that show the cache-hit rate baseline you used to decide on the change?

Best,
Alex Moreno
Platform Ops — DataSure Analytics
ops@datasure.com

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the questions. We're happy to reserve the canary slot for your staging traffic.

Plan summary for DataSure staging canary:
- Canary slot reserved: 11 June 2025, 02:00–02:30 UTC (eu-west-1a).
- Routing: We'll create a temporary route to the canary pool for the prefix you provide; please send the prefix by EOD Friday (06 Jun).
- KV-cache preservation: The runbook includes explicit KV-cache persistence checks post-handoff. We'll run a cache-hit validation step at +5 min and +20 min after each rack handoff; if hit-rates drop below 90% of baseline, we'll pause the roll and trigger rollback.
- Data/graphs: Marking Soojin to share the baseline cache-hit dashboards and the two most recent traces you requested.

Attachments: I've uploaded an abbreviated customer checklist to your account workspace and attached the latest checklist to this thread.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Planned maintenance: EU-West warm-handoff window (June 11)

Hi Alex — quick update and confirmation.

We reserved the canary slot for DataSure's staging prefix: staging.datasure.* is scheduled for the 02:00–02:30 UTC canary in eu-west-1a. Soojin has uploaded the baseline cache-hit graphs to the shared doc link below.

Two minor changes from the original note:
- Start time change: we've moved the broader region roll start from 02:30 to 02:45 UTC to allow an extended verification period after the canary. Full roll remains scheduled to finish by 06:00 UTC.
- Extra rollback guard: if any customer-specific cache-hit drops below 85% during verification we will automatically pause the roll and engage the rollback path in the runbook.

Links and attachments:
- Live updates: https://status.redwood.inference/eu-west/2025-06-11-maintenance
- Runbook: https://docs.redwood.inference/internal/runbooks/euw-warm-handoff
- Baseline graphs (uploaded): https://drive.redwood.inference/d/1Xk-cache-hit-euw-snapshots
- Attachments included here: euw-warm-handoff-runbook.pdf, kv-cache-preservation-checklist.xlsx

Please reply to confirm you received these and that the staging prefix is correct. If we don't hear back by EOD Monday we'll assume the defaults and proceed.

Thanks all — appreciate the coordination.

Markus Klein

Redwood Inference
